_meta.purpose: Single source for every number and claim in docs/pitch/deck-content.md. Edit the value here, then search deck-content.md for the fact id.

status_legend.measured_live: Measured by the team on the live Cloud Run app and reported in the deck brief. No log of the run is committed to the repo; corroborating repo sources are listed where they exist.
status_legend.repo_code: Read directly from source code in this repo.
status_legend.repo_doc: Stated in a repo document (README, ARCHITECTURE, DESIGN, spikes, research).
status_legend.regulation_verified: Marked VERIFIED in docs/research/lda-regulations.md, which means read from an official LDA or Punjab government document.
status_legend.regulation_secondary: Marked SECONDARY in docs/research/lda-regulations.md (news or property portal). Say 'reported'.
status_legend.competitor_tested: Observed in the maket.ai teardown on the free tier, 16 Oct 2026 (docs/research/maket-teardown.md).
status_legend.in_progress: Specified in docs/OVERHAUL.md or docs/design/DESIGN.md, not yet confirmed live. Confirm on the live URL before exporting the PDF, or relabel it 'Shipping next'.
status_legend.proposal: A business or roadmap idea. Not validated, and not a commitment.
status_legend.qualitative: Framing without a measured number. Keep it qualitative on slides.
status_legend.unverified: No source. Do not state as fact.

live_url.claim: The app is deployed on Cloud Run.

model_setup.claim: The setup (intake) agent runs on Gemini 3.8 Flash, with one structured call per turn that returns a brief patch and one-tap chips.
model_setup.note: Today it is not an ADK agent. The overhaul plans an 'ADK conversational setup agent' (docs/OVERHAUL.md, BACKEND track). Only call setup an ADK agent once that change is live.

model_concepts.claim: Concepts and viewport renders use Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, generating 4 in parallel. Gemini 3 Pro Image is configured for hero shots.

model_architect.claim: The planner, the builder and the ADK reviser all run on Gemini 4 Argon.

concepts_time.claim: Four photoreal concepts arrive in about 12–17 s, generated in parallel.

full_design_time.claim: A full design (plan, LDA fix loop and streamed 3D build) takes about 7 minutes.
full_design_time.note: docs/pitch/demo-script.md still says 'nobody waits 8 minutes on camera'. Update it to about 7 minutes for consistency.

code_sections_count.claim: Argon writes 23–25 code sections of House SDK code per house.

sources.where: '28 spaces, 23 code sections, 42/42 LDA checks passed'

stream_per_section.claim: Sections stream to the browser one at a time, and the viewer renders after each one.

sources.where: module docstring L5–6; SectionStream incremental parser; 'section' SSE events
§2 Stage 2: 'Sections run in order, and the viewer renders after each one'

Argon took 164 s to its first token in the one-shot spike, so the first section may not appear within seconds.

spike_oneshot_time.claim: The one-shot spike, with Argon writing raw three.js for a whole house, took 481 s in total (about 8 min). The first token arrived after 164 s.

spike_oneshot_lines.claim: The one-shot spike produced 1,780 lines (37.7k tokens).

spike_oneshot_ran_first_time.claim: The one-shot code ran first time with no console errors.

spike_oneshot_blocky.claim: The one-shot result looked blocky and low-fidelity, and it was too slow for an interactive loop. That led to the House SDK and sectioned code.

plan_max_attempts.claim: The plan fix loop sends violations back to Argon, up to 3 attempts.
plan_max_attempts.note: The overhaul adds a 'best-attempt' fix loop (docs/OVERHAUL.md, BACKEND track).

lda_check_types.claim: The deterministic LDA engine implements 18 check types: front, rear and side setbacks, the envelope, coverage, FAR, height, storeys, mumty, parapet, boundary wall, room size, clear height, daylight (8%), wet-room ventilation, room access, stairs and the overhead water tank.

sources.where: check(), L125–313: count of distinct add() ids

lda_check_types.note: Counted by hand from the code. Recount if lda.py or the overhaul's planning.py adds check types.

lda_checks_per_plan.claim: The engine runs 42–50 checks on a plan. The count scales with the number of rooms and stairs, because room and stair checks run per instance.

sources.where: per-room loop L245–292, per-stair loop L295–305

lda_checks_per_plan.note: Say 'checks', not 'rules': 18 check types are applied per room and per stair.

lda_text_version.claim: The rules come from LDA's own consolidated text of the Building & Zoning Regulations 2019, a PDF dated 09-02-2026.

fix_loop_5_1_0.claim: Argon's fix loop went from 5 violations to 1, then 0.

fix_loop_4_0.claim: On another run the fix loop went from 4 violations to 0.

livable_rules.claim: Livable-home rules: bedrooms open only to a corridor, lounge, balcony or their own bath; a stair reaches every floor including the roof; there is a railing at every drop; doors are clear of furniture; there is a clear 3 ft path to every door.

engine_invariants.claim: The engine guarantees railings, door keep-outs, the mumty door at the stair arrival, parking bays and walkways, whatever Argon writes.

self_review.claim: Argon reviews a rendered PNG of its own floor plan, with a room and area table. It critiques circulation, privacy, proportions, daylight and the brief, then revises.

sources.where: Non-negotiable 2; BACKEND track 'Argon self-review step (floor plan PNG via Pillow → critique → revise)'

audit_stair_defects.claim: An audit of three houses (two real Argon outputs and the hand-made fixture), done as a senior Lahore architect would, found stair life-safety defects in all three.
audit_stair_defects.note: The audited houses are argon-v1, the fixture and a live 1-kanal house.

audit_22ft_drop.claim: In the 1-kanal house, one roof stairwell edge had a 22 ft drop and no railing.

ibc_guards.claim: LDA does not specify guards or furniture clearances, so the spec uses IBC 2021: guards where the drop exceeds 30 in, at least 42 in high.

sources.where: §(a) item 7: no minimum for handrail height

disclaimer_pcatp.claim: Naqsha produces concept designs and a regulation pre-check. LDA requires plans to be stamped by a PCATP-registered architect.

adk_version.claim: The reviser is built on Google ADK 2.12.0.

genai_version.claim: The app uses google-genai 2.31.0; Gemini 4 Argon needs 2.30.1 or later.

adk_tools_count.claim: The ADK revision agent has 9 tools.

adk_tool_names.claim: The tool names are list_sections, read_section, get_room, check_plan_ops, apply_plan_ops, write_section, remove_section, resolve_comment and finish.

adk_revision_time.claim: One ADK revision run took about 95 s.
adk_revision_time.note: This was one run with 3 comments. The time will grow with the number of comments.

adk_window_enlarged.claim: In that run the agent enlarged a window through an LDA-checked plan edit (check_plan_ops, then apply_plan_ops).
adk_window_enlarged.note: Verbatim comment and answer are on the live 10-marla sample (comment cm_0a4b21c612eb, change ch1) and in docs/evidence/live-samples-2026-10-17.json.

adk_sofa_restyled.claim: In that run the agent restyled a sofa by rewriting a furniture section.
adk_sofa_restyled.note: Verbatim comment and answer are on the live 10-marla sample (comment cm_87e5b922d6d3, change ch3).

adk_porch_rejected.claim: The agent rejected a porch extension because of the 10 ft front setback, and offered alternatives.

sources.where: sample_10_marla.comments: cm_2581acf761a7, status rejected, verbatim resolution

adk_fallback.claim: If the ADK reviser fails, the single-shot reviser takes over. ADK saves nothing until it finishes.

comment_anchor.claim: Each comment is anchored to a room, element and level, with a snapshot. The agent receives up to 8 comment snapshots as images.

sdk_material_presets.claim: The House SDK exposes 44 PBR material presets.

sdk_furniture_types.claim: The House SDK has 57 furniture types, including Pakistani details such as ceiling fans, split ACs, a water dispenser and a prayer mat.

sdk_object_tags.claim: Every object is tagged with {layer, level, room, kind, label, id}. The tags drive layer toggles, comment anchors and the as-built check.

section_edits.claim: Edits replace whole named sections, such as furnish_g_lounge or facade_front.

asbuilt_check.claim: The as-built check confirms nothing in the 3D model projects into a mandatory open space beyond the chajja allowance: 3 ft where the open space is at least 10 ft, otherwise 1.5 ft, and 0 against a party wall.

retry_policy.claim: Shared-quota 429s and transient errors are retried with exponential backoff and jitter: 6 attempts, a 4 s initial delay, a 60 s maximum, base 2 and jitter 1.0, on status 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504. The same policy is used by google-genai and the ADK Gemini model.

degenerate_guard.claim: Streamed JSON is watched for degenerate decoding: in the last 160 characters, 2 or fewer distinct characters, or a digit repeated 40 or more times (for example 35.0000000…). Either one aborts the attempt and retries it (2 attempts). Prompts also cap numbers at 2 decimal places.

sources.where: degenerate() L20–22; NUM_RULE L13; stream_json attempts=2

detached_runs.claim: Long pipelines (design, revise) keep running if the browser disconnects. A client re-attaches through GET /api/projects/{pid}/run and replays every event.
detached_runs.note: Runs are held in memory per instance, and runs.py relies on Cloud Run session affinity. The deploy command in README.md does not show --session-affinity, so confirm the live service has it enabled.

section_repair.claim: When a section throws in the browser, the client reports the error and Argon rewrites only that section.

code_screen_patterns.claim: Before generated design.js runs, it is screened statically against 21 banned patterns: network access, import, eval and Function, DOM and window access, storage, navigator, postMessage, globals, prototype tricks, timers and location.

default_design_fallback.claim: If Argon's code is missing, a default design is built from the plan: structure, auto-furnishing for every room, landscape and lights.

one_service.claim: One Cloud Run service serves both the API and the SPA, and deploys with a single gcloud run deploy --source .

stack_cloud_run.claim: The service runs on Cloud Run in us-central1, using FastAPI and SSE, with a 3600 s request timeout.

stack_firestore.claim: Firestore stores projects, messages, versions and comments.

stack_gcs.claim: Cloud Storage holds concept images, renders and comment snapshots.

stack_vertex_global.claim: Gemini is called through Vertex AI (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) on the global endpoint, the only location that serves the newest models.

stack_identity_platform.claim: Accounts use Google Identity Platform with email and password. Google sign-in comes later.
stack_identity_platform.note: docs/design/DESIGN.md describes 'Continue with Google'. OVERHAUL.md's auth decision overrides it for this build.

auth_identity_platform.claim: Sign-up and sign-in use Identity Platform (email and password). Guests can work without an account, and signing in claims the guest's projects.

stack_bvh.claim: Walk physics (collisions and stairs) use three-mesh-bvh.

samples_endpoint.claim: Sample homes can be opened or cloned without waiting for a design run.
samples_endpoint.note: The landing page's 'Explore a sample home' button, with no sign-in, is part of the overhaul (DESIGN.md Landing).

mobile_screens.claim: The app has mobile layouts for setup, design and explore.

collab_roles.claim: Roles: Owner and Team can edit and revise, Client can comment and approve, Viewer can only look.

collab_share.claim: One Share dialog lets the owner invite Team or Client by email, or turn on a client link with Can comment or Can view.

collab_client_link.claim: The client view at /s/:token needs no account; guests give only a name. Next becomes 'Approve v2'.

collab_comment_authors.claim: Comments carry an author (name, role, colour) and threaded replies. Naqsha replies with a feasibility chip.

collab_owner_picks.claim: The owner picks which comments go into a revision. 'Include in next revision' is on by default for Team and off for Client until the owner includes it.

overhaul_scope.claim: The overhaul for the 18 Oct build covers livable rules and self-review, collaboration, day/night concepts, a per-floor program, a water tank and solar-ready roof, print to PDF, and a landing page with a Portal.

print_1_100.claim: Print to PDF produces one floor per page at 1:100, with a scale bar, a north arrow and a title block, plus cover and compliance pages.

lda_setbacks_10_30_marla.claim: In approved schemes, a 10–30 marla plot has 10 ft front, 7 ft rear and 5 ft side space on one side.

lda_coverage_10m_1k.claim: Ground coverage is 70% for 10 marla to under 1 kanal (FAR 1:2.8).

lda_height_10m_plus.claim: The maximum height is 45 ft for 10 marla and above (38 ft below 10 marla), measured from the road crown to the top of the parapet. A mumty up to 9 ft 6 in is excluded.

lda_storeys_3.claim: No plan may be approved above 3 storeys, excluding the basement, for any plot size (clause 2.7.1(a)).

lda_storeys_2020_4.claim: The 2020 text allowed 4 storeys for 10 marla and above.

lda_glazing_8pct.claim: Window glazing must be at least 8% of floor area, with half of it openable.

lda_stairs.claim: Stairs must be at least 3 ft 6 in wide, with risers of 7.5 in or less, treads of 10 in or more, and no more than 15 risers per flight.

lda_pcatp_stamp.claim: The plan must be prepared, stamped and signed by a PCATP-registered architect who is enlisted with LDA.

lda_decision_21_days.claim: LDA must decide on residential plans within 21 days in approved schemes and 30 days in controlled areas.
lda_decision_21_days.note: S1 §10.4.1 still says 45 days, so the text is inconsistent.

lda_refusal_names_rule.claim: A refusal must name the regulation breached. An appeal may be filed within 30 days.

lda_scrutiny_fee.claim: The plan scrutiny fee, for a first or revised plan, is Rs 15 per sq ft of total covered area.

lda_penalty_open_space.claim: An open-space violation on the ground floor carries a penalty of Rs 500 per sq ft.

sources.where: §2.4: compounding needs a neighbour's NOC; the text elsewhere calls these violations non-compoundable

lda_plan_scale_1_100.claim: LDA asks for building plans at 1:100 (1:200 if very large).

lda_online_since_2024.claim: LDA launched online approval of residential building plans in August 2024.
lda_online_since_2024.note: Secondary source. The system was reported shut for 10 days in May 2025 (N8), and in 2026 processing reportedly took up to 18 days (N11).

lda_amendments_aug_2026.claim: The LDA Governing Body approved further amendments on 2026-08-19. Their text has not been published.

punjab_rda_fda_gda.claim: RDA, FDA and GDA adopted the LDA 2019 text as it stood on 28-01-2020, so they still allow 4 storeys at 10 marla and above.

punjab_mda.claim: MDA has its own 2020 regulations: 38/48 ft measured to the roof, with the parapet extra, and boundary walls up to 8 ft.

punjab_dha.claim: DHA Lahore's August 2026 bylaws cap houses at 39 ft (basement, ground and first floor only).
punjab_dha.note: Check the §12.5 status labels before putting more DHA detail on a slide.

punjab_bahria.claim: Bahria Town Lahore's bylaws are not published online.

punjab_lgcd.claim: Outside the development authorities, the LG&CD Department approves building plans through e-Khidmat Markaz within 30 working days.

engine_authority_overrides.claim: The engine already accepts other authorities. DHA overrides the height to 39 ft and storeys to 2 (ground and first, plus a basement). Bahria and other authorities show the LDA baseline with a caveat.
engine_authority_overrides.note: The DHA and Bahria setbacks still use the LDA baseline. Full rule packs are on the roadmap.

maket_faq_not_ready.claim: Maket's own FAQ says its designs are not ready to build and must be checked against local requirements.

maket_plot_as_house.claim: Maket took the plot size as the house size and drew a 59′6″-wide house plus garage on a 50 ft plot, with no warning.

maket_us_centric.claim: Maket is US-centric: it offers a mudroom and mechanical room, but no drawing room, servant quarter, store, prayer room or dirty kitchen.

maket_single_floor_no_stairs.claim: Maket allows a single floor on the free tier and has no stairs anywhere.

maket_walk_no_collision.claim: Maket's walk has no collision (the tester walked through a wall) and spawns in the garage.

maket_white_box.claim: In Maket the exterior is a white box; facades exist only in renders.

maket_edit_cost.claim: Maket's AI edits by chat cost 5 credits each and are available on paid plans only.

sources.where: §2 AI edits by chat; Pricing, L32

maket_collab_view_only.claim: Maket's only collaboration is a view-only public link: no comments, no team roles and no client view.

maket_time_to_plan.claim: Going from a blank dashboard to a furnished 2D plan in Maket took about 6 minutes and about 8 user actions. Plan generation alone took about 2 minutes.
maket_time_to_plan.note: Maket reaches a 2D plan faster than Naqsha reaches a full 3D house. Speaker notes for slide 12 say so.

maket_pricing.claim: Maket's pricing: Free (30 one-time credits), Homeowner at $20/mo or $17 annual, Pro at $100/mo or $83 annual, and Scale (custom).

roadmap_rule_packs.claim: Rule packs for RDA, FDA and GDA, then DHA and Bahria Town.

discrepancies_to_resolve: Design time: the deck brief says about 7 min, and docs/pitch/demo-script.md says 'nobody waits 8 minutes'.
Check count: the brief says 42–50, while DESIGN.md and the demo script say exactly 42. Use '42–50 checks' unless the UI fixes the number.
Back-and-forth duration: README.md says 'months', and the deck brief says 'weeks'. Both are qualitative.

Runtime service account roles: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md lists aiplatform.user, datastore.user and storage.objectAdmin, while SETUP.md lists aiplatform.user, datastore.user, secretmanager.secretAccessor, logging.logWriter, cloudtrace.agent and monitoring.metricWriter. The deck names no roles.
Auth: DESIGN.md says 'Continue with Google (Firebase Auth)', and OVERHAUL.md says Identity Platform email and password now, with Google sign-in later. The deck follows OVERHAUL.md.
Setup agent: ARCHITECTURE.md calls it an ADK intake_agent, but api/app/agents/intake.py is a plain structured google-genai call. The deck does not call setup an ADK agent.
Screens: docs/screens/*.png show the v1 UI (brick accent, serif titles, numbered stage bar). DESIGN.md replaces that look. Re-shoot as v2-*.png before export.
